key_insight: Token-level credit in long-CoT RL is not uniform: highly sensitive tokens often shift without providing reliable answer-aligned learning signal, so credit should be reallocated rather than broadcast equally.
engineering_relevance: For training reasoning LLMs with RLVR, CSCR offers a low-overhead drop-in improvement over GRPO that preserves verifier direction while reducing wasted or misleading updates.
method: Measure each sampled trajectory under both correct and incorrect counterfactual outcomes.
Identify tokens with large, low-value sensitivity shifts and downweight their credit.
Renormalize token advantages to keep the original credit budget and update direction.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate on long-CoT mathematical reasoning benchmarks and report that CSCR consistently outperforms GRPO with the same number of policy updates, with ablations showing moderate downweighting works best.
watch_item: Over-modulating token credits can destabilize optimization, so the downweighting strength needs careful tuning.
paper_title: Not All Tokens Deserve Equal Credit: Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation for Long-CoT Reasoning
